To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the peak force imaging technique is the best way to detect temperature induced elastic modulus changes in supported bilayer samples, and that combining different imaging techniques can provide a more complete understanding.

phase imaging, harmonic imaging, and peak force imaging are each able to provide additional composi-tional contrast of temperature induced changes in supported bilayer patches, but the interpretation of the resulting data is not always straight-forward.
the maximum force associated with imaging the sample, or peak force, is a useful metric for characterizing mechanical properties of supported bilayers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and use of atomic force microscopy techniques for the study of biological membranes.
the application of atomic force microscopy to the investigation of temperature induced mechanical properties changes in supported bilayer systems.
the development of atomic force microscopy techniques that provide compositional contrast and/or information concerning mechanical properties of biological materials in aqueous solutions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the maximum tapping force (peak force) imaging technique is the most effective for detecting and characterizing temperature-induced changes in mechanical properties of supported lipid bilayers.
all of the techniques are useful, but the peak force imaging method is the best choice.

all techniques were able to detect the temperature induced change in the elastic modulus in the supported bilayer, however, the peak force technique was the most straightforward to interpret and provided the most direct correlation with the change in elastic modulus of TBLE.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
tapping mode AFM is capable of providing additional compositional contrast to traditional tapping mode AFMs through the use of phase imaging and higher harmonic imaging techniques.
all of the techniques used in this study are able to provide composiitional contrast consistent with the expected changes in the elastic moduli of the TBLE bilayers.

the phase imaging technique is the least useful for the study of bilayer mechanics and should be avoided for such purposes, while the peak force technique provides the most useful and direct mechanical information.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the peak force technique is the most robust of the techniques tested and is a promising tool for future investigations of the mechanical properties of supported bilayers.
the maximum tapping force (i.e., the peak force) associated to the tapping of the tip on the surface is a very good parameter to monitor mechanical changes on supported membranes.
the use of a variety of imaging techniques is necessary in order to fully characterize the surface features of a sample.
